Main.sentence: The family of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , the 44th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , is a prominent ___E:American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans)___ family active in law, education, activism and politics.

Obama's immediate family circle was the ___E:first family of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_family_of_the_United_States)___ from 2009 to 2017 during ___E:Obama's presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama)___ , and are the first such family of African-American descent.
His immediate family includes his wife ___E:Michelle Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ and daughters Malia and Sasha.

Obama's wider ancestry is made up of people of ___E:Kenyan (Luo) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people)___ , ___E:African-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American)___ , and ___E:Old Stock American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Stock_American)___ (including originally English, Scots-Irish, Welsh, German, and Swiss) ancestry.

Michelle LaVaughn Robinson Obama (born January 17, 1964) is an American lawyer, university administrator, and writer who served as the ___E:first lady of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_lady_of_the_United_States)___ from 2009 to 2017.  She is Barack Obama's wife, and was the ___E:first African-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_African-American)___ first lady. Raised on the ___E:South Side of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side_of_Chicago)___ ,  Michelle Obama is a graduate of ___E:Princeton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University)___ and ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ ,  and spent her early legal career working at the law firm ___E:Sidley Austin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidley_Austin)___ , where she met her husband.

She subsequently worked as the associate dean of Student Services at the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___  and the vice president for Community and External Affairs of the ___E:University of Chicago Medical Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Medical_Center)___ .
Barack and Michelle married in 1992.

Michelle campaigned for her ___E:husband's presidential bid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_2008_presidential_campaign)___ throughout 2007 and 2008, delivering a keynote address at the ___E:2008 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Democratic_National_Convention)___ .

She returned to speak at the ___E:2012 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Democratic_National_Convention)___ ,  and again during the ___E:2016 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Democratic_National_Convention)___ in ___E:Philadelphia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia)___ , where she delivered a speech in support of the Democratic presidential nominee, and fellow first lady, ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ .
As first lady, Michelle Obama sought to become a role model for women, an advocate for poverty awareness, education, nutrition, physical activity and healthy eating, and became a fashion icon.

Barack and Michelle Obama have two daughters: Malia Ann ( /məˈliːə/ ), born July 4, 1998,   and Natasha Marian (known as Sasha /ˈsɑːʃə/ ), born June 10, 2001.  They were both delivered at ___E:University of Chicago Medical Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Medical_Center)___ by their parents' friend and physician Anita Blanchard.

Sasha was the youngest child to reside in the White House since ___E:John F. Kennedy Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Jr.)___ arrived as an infant in 1961.  In 2014, Malia and Sasha were named two of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by Time magazine.

Before his inauguration, President Obama published an open letter to his daughters in Parade magazine, describing what he wants for them and every child in America: "to grow up in a world with no limits on your dreams and no achievements beyond your reach, and to grow into compassionate, committed women who will help build that world".
While living in Chicago, the Obamas kept busy schedules, as the Associated Press reported: "soccer, dance and drama for Malia, gymnastics and tap for Sasha, piano and tennis for both".
In July 2008, the family gave an interview to the television series Access Hollywood .
Obama later said they regretted allowing the children to be included.

Malia and Sasha both graduated from the private ___E:Sidwell Friends School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidwell_Friends_School)___ in ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , the same school that ___E:Chelsea Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton)___ , ___E:Tricia Nixon Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricia_Nixon_Cox)___ , ___E:Archibald Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archibald_Roosevelt)___ and the grandchildren of ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ (when he was ___E:Vice President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States)___ ) attended.

The Obama girls began classes there on January 5, 2009;  Malia graduated in 2016. Before the family moved to Washington in 2009, both girls attended the private ___E:University of Chicago Laboratory School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Laboratory_School)___ .
In his victory speech on the night of his election, President Obama repeated his promise to Sasha and Malia to get a puppy to take with them to the White House.

The selection was slow because Malia is allergic to animal dander;  the president subsequently said that the choice had been narrowed down to either a ___E:labradoodle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labradoodle)___ or a ___E:Portuguese Water Dog U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Water_Dog)___ , and that they hoped to find a shelter animal.

On April 12, 2009, it was reported that the Obamas had adopted a six-month-old Portuguese Water Dog given to them as a gift by Senator ___E:Ted Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy)___ ;  Malia and Sasha named the dog ___E:Bo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_(dog))___ .
The White House referred to Bo as the ___E:First Dog U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_pets)___ .
In 2013, the family adopted a second Portuguese Water Dog named ___E:Sunny U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_(dog))___ .
As a high school student, Malia Obama spent a portion of the summer in 2014 and 2015 working in television studios in New York and Los Angeles.
She spent the summer of 2016 working as an intern in the U.S.
Embassy in ___E:Madrid, Spain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid,_Spain)___ .

During the week June 26, 2016, to July 3, 2016, Michelle, Sasha, Malia, and Michelle's mother Marian Robinson went to ___E:Liberia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberia)___ to promote the Let Girls Learn Peace initiative, for which the United States has provided $27 million in aid.  They met with ___E:Ellen Johnson Sirleaf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_Johnson_Sirleaf)___ , the former ___E:president of Liberia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Liberia)___ and the first elected female head of state in Africa.

Then they went to Morocco, where they had a panel with ___E:Freida Pinto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freida_Pinto)___ and ___E:Meryl Streep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep)___ moderated by CNN's ___E:Isha Sesay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isha_Sesay)___ in Marrakesh and delivered a substantive amount of money to aid 62 million girls lacking access to formal education.
They proceeded to Spain where Michelle delivered a message about the initiative.
In August 2016, Sasha began working at Nancy's, a seafood restaurant in ___E:Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard,_Massachusetts)___ .
In the fall of 2016, Malia went on an 83-day trip to ___E:Bolivia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia)___ and ___E:Peru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru)___ .

In February 2017, Malia started an internship for ___E:Harvey Weinstein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Weinstein)___ at ___E:The Weinstein Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weinstein_Company)___ film studio in New York City.  In August 2017, Malia started attending ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ .

Sasha graduated from Sidwell Friends in 2019 and began attending the ___E:University of Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan)___ in the fall.   Sasha transferred to the ___E:University of Southern California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California)___ and graduated in 2023.
Malia graduated from Harvard in 2021 and began working as a writer on the ___E:Amazon Prime Video U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video)___ television series Swarm .

In spring 2023, ___E:Donald Glover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Glover)___ confirmed that Malia was working on a short film for his production company;  The Heart , starring ___E:Tunde Adebimpe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunde_Adebimpe)___ , was announced as part of the Short Cuts program at the ___E:2023 Toronto International Film Festival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Toronto_International_Film_Festival)___ .
Written and directed by "Malia Ann" (her credited name), the film screened at the ___E:2024 Sundance Film Festival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sundance_Film_Festival)___ .
___E:Marian Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_Robinson)___ , Michelle Obama's mother, resided in the White House during the Obama presidency.

Barack Obama was raised by his mother, ___E:Stanley Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham)___ , and maternal grandparents ___E:Madelyn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelyn_Dunham)___ and ___E:Stanley Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham)___ .
He often referred to his family during his candidacy and two terms as president.
Obama's maternal heritage consists mostly of English ancestry, with smaller amounts of ___E:German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_American)___ , Scotch-Irish, Welsh, and Swiss ancestry.

Research by a genealogy team at ___E:Ancestry.com U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancestry.com)___ , published in 2012, stated that Obama is likely descended from the African slave ___E:John Punch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Punch_(slave))___ through his mother's Bunch line, with generations of African Americans who gradually "married white" and became landowners in colonial Virginia.
The Bunches later moved to Tennessee; in 1834 a daughter moved to Kansas, where Obama's mother was born four generations later.
Obama's mother was born Stanley Ann Dunham.
She became an anthropologist, specializing in economic anthropology and rural development.

She earned her ___E:PhD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy)___ degree from the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ and worked with the ___E:United States Agency for International Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development)___ , the ___E:Ford Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Foundation)___ , and Women's World Banking, to promote the use of ___E:microcredit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcredit)___ in order to combat global poverty.

The Ann Dunham Soetoro Endowment in the Anthropology Department at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and the Ann Dunham Soetoro Graduate Fellowships at the ___E:East–West Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East%E2%80%93West_Center)___ (EWC) in ___E:Honolulu, Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu,_Hawaii)___ , are named in her honor.
Obama has said that his mother was the dominant figure of his formative years. "The values she taught me continue to be my touchstone when it comes to how I go about the world of politics."
Stanley Armour Dunham is the maternal grandfather of Barack Obama.

He served as a ___E:sergeant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergeant)___ in the ___E:U.S. Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army)___ during World War II, enlisting just after the attacks on ___E:Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor)___ .
He and his wife Madelyn Dunham raised Obama in Honolulu, Hawaii.

In addition to Obama, Stanley is related to six US presidents: ___E:James Madison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison)___ , ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ , ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ , ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ , ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ , and ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ .
He died in Honolulu, Hawaii, and is buried at the ___E:Punchbowl National Cemetery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punchbowl_National_Cemetery)___ .
Madelyn Dunham (née Madelyn Lee Payne) was Obama's maternal grandmother who worked in banking and became vice president of a bank in Hawaii.

Obama grew up with her and remembered that when he was a child, his grandmother "read me the opening lines of the ___E:Declaration of Independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence)___ and told me about the men and women who marched for equality because they believed those words put to paper two centuries ago should mean something."
Charles Thomas Payne is Madelyn Dunham's younger brother and Obama's great-uncle.
He was born in 1925. Payne served during World War II in the U.S.
Army ___E:89th Infantry Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/89th_Division_(United_States))___ .
Obama has often described Payne's role in liberating the ___E:Ohrdruf forced labor camp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohrdruf_forced_labor_camp)___ .
There was brief media attention when Obama mistakenly identified the camp as ___E:Auschwitz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz_concentration_camp)___ during the campaign.
In 2009, Payne spoke about his war experience:
Ohrdruf was in that string of towns going across, south of ___E:Gotha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotha)___ and ___E:Erfurt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erfurt)___ .
Our division was the first one in there.
When we arrived there were no German soldiers anywhere around that I knew about.
There was no fighting against the Germans, no camp guards.
The whole area was overrun by people from the camp dressed in the most pitiful rags, and most of them were in a bad state of starvation.
Payne appeared in the visitor's gallery at the Democratic National Convention in Denver, Colorado, when his great-nephew was nominated for President.
He was the assistant director of the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ 's Library.
Ralph Dunham was Stanley Dunham's older brother and Obama's great-uncle, who served in the U.S.

Army as an assignment and personnel officer during World War II. He landed at Normandy's Omaha Easy Red Beach on D-Day plus four, and moved with troops in the fighting through France, Italy and Germany.
Eleanor Dunham, Obama's great-aunt, was the younger sister of Stanley Armour Dunham and Ralph Dunham.
Married to Ralph Lee Berkebile.
She was the youngest daughter of Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham Sr. and his second wife, Martha Mae Stonehouse.
She retired from civil service as an executive secretary. [citation needed]
Margaret Arlene Payne, Obama's great-aunt, was the younger sister of Madelyn Dunham and Charles Payne.

She was a professor of nutrition who taught at the ___E:University of Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Missouri)___ , Kansas City, and at the ___E:University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina_at_Chapel_Hill)___ (1980–1990).
She wrote numerous research articles and two books.
Obama's family said that his maternal great-grandmother, Leona McCurry, was part Native American.
She reportedly held that as a "source of considerable shame" and "blanched whenever someone mentioned the subject and hoped to carry the secret to her grave".

But her daughter Madelyn Dunham (Obama's maternal grandmother) "would turn her head in profile to show off her beaked nose, which along with a pair of jet-black eyes, was offered as proof of ___E:Cherokee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee)___ blood".
To date, no concrete evidence has surfaced of Cherokee heritage in the McCurry line.
Obama's family said that his paternal great-grandmother, Ruth Dunham, died November 26, 1926, from ___E:ptomaine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ptomaine)___ poisoning.
She resided in Topeka, Kansas.
A maternal 3rd great-grandfather of Barack Obama, nicknamed "Fully".

Born c. 1829 in ___E:Moneygall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneygall)___ , ___E:King's County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Offaly)___ , Ireland, he emigrated to Ohio via New York in 1850, making him the most recent immigrant on the maternal side of Barack Obama's family tree. Fulmoth married Charlotte Holloway and raised a family which included three daughters (including Mary Ann).
She and two of her sisters married three Dunham brothers.
Kearney and his wife are buried in Fairview Cemetery in ___E:Labette County, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labette_County,_Kansas)___ .
Descendants placed a headstone there in 2014.  Around the same time, a photo of him was discovered.

Barack Obama visited Moneygall in 2011.  In 2014, " ___E:Barack Obama Plaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Plaza)___ ", a ___E:service station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorway_service_area)___ and visitor center, was opened in Moneygall.
In 2015, a photograph of Kearney was discovered and made publicly available.
In 2018, statues of Michelle and Barack were erected in Moneygall.
Lolo Soetoro, Javanese given name: Martodihardjo ,   was the second husband of Ann Dunham (married on March 15, 1965)  and stepfather to Barack Obama.
He is Maya Soetoro-Ng's father.
After his divorce from Dunham, Soetoro married Erna Kustina.
They had two children, Yusuf Aji Soetoro (b. 1981) and Rahayu Nurmaida Soetoro (b. 1984).
Maya Soetoro-Ng, Obama's half-sister, was born in ___E:Jakarta, Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta,_Indonesia)___ .
She has a half-brother and half-sister, Yusuf and Aya Soetoro, from her father's second marriage.
She is married to Canadian-American Konrad Ng, with whom she has two daughters, Suhaila and Savita.
Maya Soetoro-Ng is a teacher in Hawaii.

Konrad Ng is Barack Obama's brother-in-law. He is of ___E:Malaysian Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_Chinese)___ descent,  and his parents are from ___E:Kudat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kudat)___ and ___E:Sandakan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandakan)___ , two small towns in ___E:Sabah, Malaysia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabah,_Malaysia)___ .
Ng and his younger brother, Perry, were born and raised in ___E:Burlington, Ontario U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Ontario)___ , Canada.
Perry Ng works for the ___E:University of Ottawa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ottawa)___ .
He married Maya Soetoro-Ng at the end of 2003 in Hawaii.
They have two daughters, Suhaila    and Savita.
Konrad Ng is a U.S. citizen.
He was an assistant professor at the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi)___ 's Academy of Creative Media.
From 2011 to 2015, he was the Director of the Smithsonian's ___E:Asian Pacific American Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Asian_Pacific_American_Center)___ .
Since 2016, he has been the Executive Director of The ___E:Shangri La U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shangri_La_(Doris_Duke))___ Museum of Islamic Art, Culture & Design in Honolulu.

He studied philosophy at ___E:McGill University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGill_University)___ and cultural studies at the ___E:University of Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Victoria)___ before getting his PhD degree from ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ .
Ng studies "how minority and diaspora communities use cinema and digital media to engage in artistic and cultural representation and preservation, and community mobilization".
From 2011 to 2016, he served as director of the ___E:Smithsonian Asian Pacific American Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Asian_Pacific_American_Center)___ .
Robert Wolfley, born in 1835, is one of Obama's maternal third great-grandfathers.

He served as a private in Company A, ___E:145th Ohio Infantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/145th_Ohio_Infantry)___ during the ___E:American Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ .
He died July 17, 1895, and is buried in the Olathe Memorial Cemetery in ___E:Olathe, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olathe,_Kansas)___ .

According to ___E:Ancestry.com U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancestry.com)___ 's research in 2012, using a combination of historical documents and ___E:yDNA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YDNA)___ analysis, genealogists found that ___E:John Punch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Punch_(slave))___ , the first documented African slave in the ___E:Colony of Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Virginia)___ , has been documented as likely an eleventh great-grandfather of Obama through his mother, Ann Dunham, and her Bunch ancestors.
With intermarriage, there were eventually both white and African-American lines of descent from Punch; some Bunch descendants were classified as white by the early 18th century.

Other Bunch descendants were considered ___E:free people of color U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_people_of_color)___ . ___E:Ralph Bunche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Bunche)___ , American delegate to the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ , is thought by historian Paul Heinegg to have likely been an African-American descendant of the Bunch family via South Carolina and ___E:Detroit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit)___ , Michigan.

Jonathan Singletary Dunham, born in 1640 in the ___E:Massachusetts Bay Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Bay_Colony)___ , was one of Obama's maternal eighth great-grandfathers and is his earliest ancestor known to be born in North America.

Obama's family in Kenya are members of the ___E:Jok'Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jok%27Obama&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , a clan belonging to the ___E:Luo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_(Kenya_and_Tanzania))___ people, the nation's second-largest ethnic group.
Linguistically, ___E:Luo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dholuo)___ is one of the ___E:Nilotic languages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_languages)___ .
The Obama family is concentrated in the western Kenyan province of ___E:Nyanza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyanza_Province)___ .
Paternal grandfather to Barack Obama, he was born Onyango Obama.
One source gives 1870–1975 as his dates of birth and death, possibly based on his tombstone in his home village.

His probate record shows a death date of 28th November 1975.  Barack Obama relates finding in 1988 a British document, based on a 1928 ordinance, recording his grandfather as 35 years old. The date of the document was estimated to be about 1930, which would mean that his grandfather had been born c. 1895 .  ) The Luo are given names related to the circumstances of their birth, and Onyango means "born in the early morning".
Onyango was the fifth son of his mother, Nyaoke, who was the first of the five wives of his father, Obama.

Barack Obama relates how his step-grandmother Granny Sarah ( ___E:Sarah Onyango Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org#Sarah_Onyango_Obama)___ ) describes his grandfather: "Even from the time that he was a boy, your grandfather Onyango was strange.

It is said of him that he had ants up his anus, because he could not sit still."  As a young man, Onyango learned to speak, read and write in English, the language of British colonial administration in Kenya.
Onyango worked as a mission cook and as a local ___E:herbalist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbalist)___ .
He joined the ___E:King's African Rifles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King%27s_African_Rifles)___ during World War I.
In 1949, Onyango spent at least six months in ___E:Kamiti Prison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamiti_Maximum_Security_Prison)___ .
He was tried in a magistrates' court either on charges of ___E:sedition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition)___ or being a member of a banned organization.
Records do not survive; all such documentation was routinely destroyed after six years by the colonial administration.

Onyango was then subject to ___E:torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture)___ due to suspicions that he was an associate of the ___E:Mau Mau rebels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_Rebellion)___ .
In his memoir, Obama recounted family descriptions of his grandfather's shocking physical state when released from prison:
"When he returned to ___E:Alego U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siaya_District)___ he was very thin and dirty.
He had difficulty walking, and his head was full of ___E:lice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_lice)___ ." For some time, he was too traumatized to speak about his experiences.
His wife told his grandson Obama: "From that day on, I saw that he was now an old man."
Onyango was permanently scarred, suffering pain and requiring assistance in moving until his death.
Although previously he had worked closely with the British, Onyango became bitterly anglophobic after his experiences in Kamiti Prison.

According to his third wife, Sarah, Onyango had converted from tribal religion to ___E:Roman Catholicism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ early in life. When ___E:Seventh-day Adventist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church)___ ___E:missionaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missionary)___ visited the ___E:Kendu Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendu_Bay)___ area many people were baptized into the church, including Onyango.
When he later converted to Islam, he took the first name Hussein .
She said that he passed on the name of Hussein to his children, but not the religion.
Onyango is sometimes referred to as Mzee Hussein Onyango Obama.
The word mzee (meaning "elder") is a Kenyan ___E:honorific U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorific)___ .
To this day the Obama family in Kenya is divided between Seventh-day Adventists and Muslims.
Also known as Akumu Nyanjoga and Sje.     She was Barack Obama's ___E:paternal grandmother U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paternal_grandmother)___ , and the second wife of Hussein Onyango Obama.
She had three children with Onyango: daughters Sarah and Auma, and son Barack (Barack Obama's father).
Her father was named Njango or Njoga,  and she was born and raised in the Western Kenyan village of ___E:Karabondi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachuonyo_Constituency)___ .

In his memoir Dreams from My Father , Obama wrote that Akumu was miserable in her marriage and abandoned Onyango Obama and her children with him. She subsequently married again and moved to Tanganyika, now ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ .
Her name Akumu means "mysterious birth".
Her mother conceived her after having given birth to another child and before resuming her ___E:menses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menses)___ .
Akumu took the name Habiba upon her conversion to Islam in her second marriage, to Salmin Orinda, a Muslim from Wagwe, near Homa Hills, South Nyanza.

Born and raised in ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ , Kenya,  he earned a degree in ___E:accounting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accounting)___ from the ___E:University of Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nairobi)___ .

Born Ruth Beatrice Baker in the United States c. 1937 , the daughter of Maurice Joseph Baker and Ida Baker of ___E:Newton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Massachusetts)___ , who are of ___E:Lithuanian-Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_Jews)___ descent.

Mark was educated in the US, graduating from ___E:Brown University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_University)___ ; he studied ___E:physics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics)___ at ___E:Stanford University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University)___ , and received an ___E:MBA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration)___ degree from ___E:Emory University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emory_University)___ .

Barack Obama's half-brother (also known as David Opiyo Obama ), son of Barack Obama Sr. and his third wife, Ruth Baker, an American.

Youngest half-brother of Barack Obama, born c. May 1982, son of Barack Obama Sr.  and Jael Otieno. (She has since moved to ___E:Atlanta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta)___ , Georgia as a full-time resident.)   George was six months old when his father died in an automobile accident, after which he was raised in Nairobi by his mother and a French stepfather.
His mother took him to South Korea for two years while she was working there.

Returning to Kenya, George Obama "slept rough for several years",  until his aunt gave him a six-by-eight foot corrugated metal shack in the ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ slum of ___E:Huruma Flats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huruma_Flats)___ .
As of August 2008, George Obama was studying to become a mechanic.
He received little attention until featured in an article in the Italian-language edition of Vanity Fair in August 2008 during the US presidential campaign.
This portrayed him as living in poverty, shame, and obscurity.
The article quoted George Obama as saying that he lived "on less than a dollar a month" and said that he "does not mention his famous half-brother in conversation" out of shame at his own poverty.
In later interviews, George contradicted this account.
In an interview with The Times , he "said that he was furious at subsequent reports that he had been abandoned by the Obama family and that he was filled with shame about living in a slum".

He told The Times , "Life in Huruma is good." George Obama said that he expects no favors, that he was supported by relatives, and that reports he lived on a dollar a month were "all lies by people who don't want my brother to win".
He told The Telegraph that he was inspired by his half-brother.

According to Time , George "has repeatedly denied ... that he feels abandoned by Obama".  ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ quoted him as saying, "I was brought up well. I live well even now. The magazines, they have exaggerated everything – I think I kind of like it here. There are some challenges, but maybe it is just like where you come from, there are the same challenges."  George Obama and the British journalist Damien Lewis published George's story in a 2011 book called Homeland .
George also appeared in the 2012 film, 2016: Obama's America , an anti-Obama documentary.
At times using a variation of the name of his father, Onyango Obama ,   Omar Okech Obama is a half-uncle of Barack Obama.

Born on June 3, 1944, in ___E:Nyang'oma Kogelo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang%27oma_Kogelo)___ , he is the eldest son of ___E:Onyango U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyango_Obama)___ and his third wife, ___E:Sarah Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Onyango_Obama)___ .

He moved to the United States in October 1963 when he was 17 years old as part of Kenya president ___E:Tom Mboya's Airlift Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya#Political_life)___ project, to send promising Kenyan students to the US for education, particularly undergraduate and graduate school.

Once he arrived in the country, his half-brother, Barack Obama Sr., found him a place at a boys' school then known as Browne & Nichols, in ___E:Cambridge, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts)___ .
He later dropped out of school and changed his name to O. Onyango Obama.

He has operated a liquor store in ___E:Framingham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Framingham,_Massachusetts)___ , where he resided as of March 2011.   Barack Obama lived with Onyango in the 1980s while a student at Harvard Law School in Cambridge.

Omar Okech Obama was subject to a ___E:deportation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportation)___ order in 1989.  After an unsuccessful appeal, he was given a new deportation order in 1992.   He was arrested on August 24, 2011, for ___E:driving under the influence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence)___ , or DUI,  and was held in jail until September 9, 2011, on a federal immigration warrant.
The Boston Herald reported in August 2011 that Obama had had a valid Social Security card "for at least 19 years".

On November 30, 2012, the ___E:Board of Immigration Appeals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Immigration_Appeals)___ remanded the immigration case to the ___E:Executive Office for Immigration Review U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Office_for_Immigration_Review)___ for reconsideration of the original order of deportation, which was issued in 1986 and re-issued in 1992.
An immigration judge ruled on January 30, 2013, that Onyango Obama would receive a deportation hearing.

Onyango's attorneys said that his defense at the December 3, 2013, deportation hearing would be a reliance on the ___E:Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_Reform_and_Control_Act_of_1986)___ , because Onyango had resided in the U.S. since before January 1, 1972, the cutoff date of the 1986 ___E:amnesty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty)___ .

At the hearing, Immigration Judge Leonard I. Shapiro ruled that Onyango was eligible for ___E:permanent residence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_residence_(United_States))___ and would receive a ___E:green card U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_residence_(United_States))___ .
___E:Zeituni Onyango U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeituni_Onyango)___ , half-aunt of Barack Obama,  was born May 29, 1952, in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ .
Onyango is referred to as "Aunti Zeituni" in Obama's memoir Dreams from My Father .
She entered the US in 2000 on a temporary visa with her son who was going to school; she applied in 2002 for political asylum due to unrest in Kenya and ethnic conflict.

She was granted asylum in 2010. She died on April 7, 2014, from complications caused by cancer and respiratory problems.
Barack Obama has called his wife ___E:Michelle Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ "the most quintessentially American woman I know".

Her family is of African-American heritage, descendants of Africans and Europeans of the ___E:colonial era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_history_of_the_United_States)___ and ___E:antebellum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antebellum_United_States)___ eras.  Michelle Obama's family history traces from colonists and ___E:slavery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States)___ in the South to ___E:Reconstruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era_of_the_United_States)___ to the ___E:Great Migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ to northern cities, in her family's case, Cleveland and Chicago.
Each of her four grandparents was multiracial.
Some of Michelle's relatives still reside in ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ .
Extended family from her mother's Shields ancestors also reside in Georgia and throughout the South.

Michelle's earliest known relative on her father's side is her great-great grandfather Jim Robinson, born in the 1850s, who was an American ___E:slave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery)___ on the ___E:Friendfield Plantation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendfield_Plantation)___ in ___E:Georgetown, South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown,_South_Carolina)___ in the ___E:Low Country U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Lowcountry)___ , where African Americans developed as the ___E:Gullah people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gullah_people)___ and culture.

The family believes that after the Civil War, he worked as a Friendfield ___E:sharecropper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharecropper)___ for the rest of his life. He is said to have been buried there in an unmarked grave.
Jim married twice, first to a woman named Louiser, with whom he had two sons, Gabriel and Fraser, Michelle Obama's great-grandfather.
A daughter was born to the family, but her name has not been discovered, and she is believed to have died as a child.
His second marriage to Rose Ella Cohen produced six more children.
Fraser had an arm amputated as a result of a boyhood injury.
He worked as a shoemaker, a newspaper salesman, and in a lumber mill.  Carrie Nelson, Gabriel Robinson's daughter, is the keeper of family lore and the oldest living Robinson at 80 years old in 2008.
At least three of Michelle Obama's great-uncles served in the ___E:military of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_United_States)___ .

One aunt moved to ___E:Princeton, New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton,_New_Jersey)___ , where she worked as a maid. She cooked ___E:Southern-style meals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_food)___ for Michelle and her brother Craig, when they were students at ___E:Princeton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University)___ .

The earliest known relative on her mother's side is her great-great-great-grandmother, Melvinia Shields (1844–1938), who was held as a slave on a farm in ___E:Clayton County, North Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton_County,_Georgia)___ .
Her master was Henry Walls Shields, who had a 200-acre farm near ___E:Rex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex,_Georgia)___ .
He would have worked along with his slaves.
Melvinia became pregnant at about age 15 and had a biracial son, Dolphus T. Shields, born into slavery about 1860. Melvinia did not talk to relatives about his father.
Based on DNA and other evidence, in 2012 researchers said the father was likely 20-year-old Charles Marion Shields, son of Melvinia's master.
After the Civil War, Dolphus Shields moved to ___E:Birmingham, Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham,_Alabama)___ .
Charles later became a teacher and married a white woman.
Michelle Obama's extended family has said that people didn't talk about slavery time while they were growing up.  Michelle Obama's distant ancestry also includes Irish and other European roots.

On June 26, 2012, a monument to Shields was erected in Rex, with an inscription summarizing her life and "a five-generation journey that began in oppression" resulting in her descendant becoming First Lady of the United States.
A year later, the monument was vandalized and knocked from its base, but was quickly replaced.

Marian Lois Robinson (born Marian Lois Shields, July 30, 1937, died May 31, 2024), was descended from Dolphus Shields and his wife. She married Michelle's father, ___E:Fraser Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraser_Robinson)___ , on October 27, 1960. Some media outlets dubbed Robinson as the "First Granny".
Marian took Sasha and Malia to school daily.
The Obamas announced her death on May 31, 2024.

Michelle Obama's father (August 1, 1935 — March 6, 1991), married Michelle's mother, ___E:Marian Shields U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_Shields_Robinson)___ , on October 27, 1960.   Robinson was a pump worker at the City of Chicago water plant.

Craig Robinson, Michelle Obama's brother, was born in 1962. From 2008 until 2014, he served as ___E:head coach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_coach)___ of men's basketball at ___E:Oregon State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_State_Beavers_men%27s_basketball)___ .

Michelle Obama's paternal grandmother (February 6, 1915 – September 17, 2002) and married to Fraser Robinson Jr. She was born in Chicago, Illinois, to James Preston Johnson (1880–1920?) and Phoebe (1879–1920?).
Robbie Shields Terry (born Robbie Lee Shields; July 3, 1908 – June 1, 1983) was Michelle Obama's great-aunt: her mother's father's sister.
In the 1940 census, she was listed as head of household,  with ___E:Marian Shields U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_Shields_Robinson)___ listed as niece.

Her nuclear family moved into a small apartment on the second floor in their house while she was still a young child.
Robbie was Michelle's piano teacher  as well as nearest neighbor.

When she died, Robbie, a widow, left the house to her mother, ___E:Marian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_Shields_Robinson)___ , and father, ___E:Fraser Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraser_Robinson)___ , who moved downstairs.

When Barack Obama settled in Chicago after graduating law school, he moved into this same apartment.

Capers C. Funnye Jr. is Michelle Obama's first cousin once removed: his mother, Verdelle Robinson Funnye (born Verdelle Robinson; August 22, 1930 – April 16, 2000), was a sister of Michelle Obama's paternal grandfather, Fraser Robinson Jr. He is 12 years older, and Funnye and Obama grew to know each other as adults in Chicago, where both were involved in community organizing, along with Barack Obama.

He is one of America's most prominent African-American rabbis, known for acting as a bridge between mainstream Jewry and African American Jews. He converted to Judaism after 1970, during years of activism when he regarded Christianity as having been imposed on slaves.
